UN leadership candidate Grynspan vows peacemaking and reform

April 22 - Former Costa Rican vice president Rebeca Grynspan, a candidate to head the United Nations, vowed on Wednesday that peacemaking would be her first priority if chosen, while warning that trust is waning in the world body and time running out to restore it. "Peacemaking is the purpose of this organization," Grynspan, one of four candidates vying to become the next U.N. secretary-general from next year, told a hearing on her candidacy at the U.N. in New York. "I will be a peacemaker. I will land before conflicts erupt, be the first to pick up the phone. I will travel to where the wars are. I will speak to every party. I will work with the Security Council, with the member states, and will mediate among the mediators," she said. The candidates are bidding for a five-year term to succeed Antonio Guterres of Portugal, which can be extended for another five, and will face an enormous task to revitalize an organization in crisis, whose stature has significantly diminished in recent years. Major powers, even as they increasingly flout long-held norms of international order, have pressed the 193-member organization to reform, slash costs, and prove its relevance. There are far fewer candidates than in 2016, when Guterres was chosen from a field of 13 contenders, but others can join in coming months. Born to parents who fled Europe after World War Two, Grynspan said their lives and her experience had been a demonstration of what peace makes possible. Grynspan, an economist who is the current head of the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development, also vowed to lead reform efforts. "To defend the United Nations today is to have the courage to change it. Reform for delivery will be my second priority," she said, adding that "trust in the organization is waning, and ... time is running out to restore it."
NO WOMAN HAS LED U.N. Grynspan, 70, is aiming to be the first woman to head the U.N. in its 80-year history.

Being a UN member means that a country can participate in UN decisions, adhere to the UN Charter, and access UN programmes and support. In the UNGA, the rule is: one country, one vote for the delegations that come from every member state. Admission to the UN is not the same as diplomatic recognition by other countries. To become a full UN member, a country has to follow these steps:
The country applies to the UN secretary-general, declaring that it accepts the UN Charter and will fulfil its duties. The UNSC, which comprises five permanent members (China, France, Russia, the UK, and the US) and 10 non-permanent members (rotated every two years), reviews the application. Admission requires at least nine affirmative votes and no vetoes from any permanent member. If the UNSC recommends admission, the UNGA must approve it with a two-thirds majority. Once approved, the country becomes a full UN member, gaining full rights and broader international recognition. Its flag is added to the UN headquarters, and it is entitled to participate fully in all UN activities, including voting in the UNGA. How the US has used its veto to block full UN membership for Palestine
In 2012, the UNGA upgraded Palestine’s status from an observer entity to a non-member observer state. This change did not make Palestine a full UN member, so it cannot vote on resolutions, but it can attend meetings and participate in debates. On April 18, 2024, the US vetoed a widely supported resolution in the UNGA that would have granted Palestine full UN membership, blocking the upgrade despite broad international backing.

The UNGA also debates matters of human rights, international law and cooperation in “economic, social, cultural, educational, and health fields”. Operationally, the UNGA approves the UN’s sprawling annual budget, with one of its six main committees managing the funding of 11 active peacekeeping missions around the world. Baerbock got 167 votes, almost double the 88 votes needed to win, while high-ranking German diplomat Helga Schmid received 7 votes as a write-in and 14 countries abstained. Three men pleaded guilty on Wednesday, while three others entered their guilty pleas earlier in the week. Adam Charles Palermo, 40, of Rampart Village; Ismael Vega, 41, of Westlake; and Yachua Mauricio Flores, 23, of Lincoln Heights were part of a group of protestors who lit cardboard and vegetation on fire, as well as fireworks, and dropped them from the freeway overpass, targeting a CHP vehicle, according to prosecutors. The vehicle caught fire. Flores also poured a liquid on the flames, igniting them further. Palermo pleaded guilty to one felony count of assaulting, resisting, and impeding persons assisting federal officers and employees with a deadly or dangerous weapon. He faces a statutory maximum of 20 years in federal prison. Vega and Flores each pleaded guilty to one felony count of obstructing, impeding, and interfering with law enforcement during a civil disorder. Both face a statutory maximum sentence of five years in federal prison. Balton Montion, 25, LA County resident at the time, Ronald Alexis Coreas, 23, of Westlake and Junior Roldan, 27, of Hollywood, threw rocks at law enforcement officers who attempted to clear the freeway overpass. Coreas and Roldan each pleaded guilty to one misdemeanor count of simple assault on a person assisting a federal officer. Each faces a statutory maximum of one year in federal prison. Montion pleaded guilty to one felony count of obstructing, impeding, and interfering with law enforcement during a civil disorder.

# Forecast log — 2026-05-19

## State audit

- `state.json` remains absent; used the refreshed `market.csv`, persistent notes, the dated prediction archive, and date-capped news search.
- Market: 378 total, 162 active, 216 resolved.
- Coverage before and after updates: 162/162 active questions had forecasts; no net new active question opened.
- Five questions resolved since the prior session:
  - q250786: Tokyo Verdy Beleza; forecast 0.57 — hit.
  - q444151: Jose Mourinho; forecast 0.985 — hit.
  - q602042: SPCX; forecast 0.97 — hit.
  - q515929: `Sultan Ibrahim`; forecast `Sultan Ibrahim Iskandar` at 0.52 — right person, likely an exact-string miss.
  - q740282: Dharmendra Pradhan; forecast led with Surya Kant at 0.80 and assigned Pradhan 0.01 — miss. The movement's origin was less predictive than the rally's stated employment, education, and governance demands.

## May 19 evidence

- Searched all 162 active question titles against May 19 reporting and ran targeted follow-ups on direct matches and imminent contracts.
- q891597: 41 flotilla vessels were intercepted after the mission sailed from Marmaris. Turkey said it was coordinating detainees' safe return with relevant countries; its operational role and 2025 repatriation precedent strengthened it further.
- q796483: Bruno Fernandes won the FWA Footballer of the Year award, finished ahead of Declan Rice and Erling Haaland, and equalled the Premier League single-season record with 20 assists—nine more than the next player. Arsenal's confirmed title keeps Rice the main alternative, but Fernandes is now the clear official-league-award favorite.
- q195361: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi made 93 from 38 balls, moved atop the Orange Cap table with 579 runs at a strike rate above 237, and collected his third player-of-the-match award. His two earlier matches against Hyderabad temper the increase: SRH won both, with Ishan Kishan making 91 and 74.
- q864352: Israel issued displacement threats to 12 additional southern localities, explicitly including Nabatieh At-Tahta, while recent strikes concentrated on the Nabatieh district. This moved Nabatieh narrowly ahead of Tyre for a subsequent whole-city order.
- q782824: Paramount leadership is discussing reducing Bari Weiss's day-to-day control of *60 Minutes* and installing an unnamed, more experienced television executive. This sharply reduced Weiss as a conceivable appointment and modestly strengthened experienced internal candidates.
- No same-day evidence warranted changing the other 157 active forecasts.

## Submissions

- q891597: Turkey 0.82; Jordan 0.09; South Africa 0.03; Qatar 0.02; Tunisia 0.015.
- q796483: Bruno Fernandes 0.58; Declan Rice 0.28; Erling Haaland 0.075; Bukayo Saka 0.03; Viktor Gyokeres 0.02.
- q195361: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi 0.34; Ishan Kishan 0.20; Abhishek Sharma 0.12; Yashasvi Jaiswal 0.11; Heinrich Klaasen 0.10.
- q864352: Nabatieh 0.48; Tyre 0.39; Bint Jbeil 0.045; Baalbek 0.025; Sidon 0.02.
- q782824: Guy Campanile 0.23; Shachar Bar-On 0.18; Tom Cibrowski 0.11; Adam Yamaguchi 0.09; Bari Weiss 0.01.

## Calibration notes

- Do not overfit to the incident that founded a movement when the resolution asks about a later rally's demand. The issue portfolio and explicit rally framing can dominate the origin story.
- Open-answer scoring again appears exact-string sensitive. Prefer the shortest common public name unless the question explicitly requires a legal or expanded name.
- A related award plus a near-record or record statistical season is strong evidence for an official player award, even when the title-winning team supplies the main rival.
- In a single-match player market, recent form should move probabilities only moderately; opponent-specific history and the large tail of possible match winners remain important.

# Forecast log — 2026-05-20

## State audit

- `state.json` remains absent; used the refreshed `market.csv`, the dated prediction archive, persistent notes, and date-capped news search.
- Market: 378 total, 159 active, 219 resolved. Coverage before updates was 159/159 active questions, with no uncovered new contract.
- Three questions resolved since the prior session:
  - q14338: `NASCAR All-Star race`; forecast led with Cracker Barrel 400 at 0.80 — miss. The realized final appearance mattered, not the last scheduled points race.
  - q891597: `Turkiye`; forecast `Turkey` at 0.82 — right country, exact-string miss.
  - q896840: `Al-Nassr`; forecast `Al Nassr` at 0.84 — right club, exact-string miss.

## May 20 evidence

- Searched all 159 active titles against May 20 reporting and ran targeted follow-ups on direct matches and imminent contracts.
- q984668: a fresh Invamer poll put Ivan Cepeda at 44.3%, versus 21.5% for Abelardo De la Espriella and 19.8% for Paloma Valencia, only eleven days before the first round. Cepeda is overwhelmingly likely to lead the count.
- q713763: Amanda Blanc is BP's senior independent director and led the search that appointed chair Albert Manifold. That governance role makes her the clear default interim chair if the position becomes vacant.
- q188803: Kimi Antonelli leads George Russell by 20 points before Canada's first sprint weekend. Russell has an unusually strong Montreal record, so his chance of overcoming the deficit is material but still only about one in ten.
- q165056: Charles Leclerc enters Canada third on 63 points, 12 ahead of Lando Norris and 14 ahead of Lewis Hamilton. McLaren's Miami sprint one-two and planned upgrades strengthen Norris and Oscar Piastri, but Leclerc remains favored to retain third.
- q384398: Qatar publicly said the US-Iran negotiations need more time, while Oman is engaged on the Strait of Hormuz mechanism. This modestly strengthened Qatar and Oman as the country mediating alongside Pakistan.
- q388712: May 20 reporting confirmed that the US plans to shrink its NATO Force Model contribution at a May 22 Brussels meeting, but said the force composition remains secret; probabilities were retained while repairing the required comma-separated answer format.
- q105885: probabilities were retained while repairing the explicitly required comma-separated country-pair format.
- Same-day Lebanon strikes, Sudan fighting, India demolitions, and the Shreyas Iyer endorsement did not move their related contracts enough to justify revisions.

## Submissions

- q984668: Ivan Cepeda 0.95; Abelardo De la Espriella 0.026; Paloma Valencia 0.02.
- q713763: Amanda Blanc 0.84; Melody Meyer 0.07; Pamela Daley 0.035; Tushar Morzaria 0.02.
- q188803: Kimi Antonelli 0.90; George Russell 0.10.
- q165056: Charles Leclerc 0.55; Lando Norris 0.22; Lewis Hamilton 0.09; Oscar Piastri 0.055; George Russell 0.04.
- q388712: `F-35, F-16` 0.55; `F-15, F-16` 0.15; `F-35, F-15` 0.10.
- q384398: Qatar 0.48; Oman 0.27; Turkiye 0.10; Saudi Arabia 0.045; United Arab Emirates 0.02.
- q105885: `China, Turkiye` 0.18; `China, Cuba` 0.15; `Colombia, Mexico` 0.14; `Russia, China` 0.12; `Cuba, Colombia` 0.08.

## Calibration notes

- Treat accepted-answer formatting as part of the forecast. Semantic equivalence did not rescue `Turkey` versus `Turkiye` or `Al Nassr` versus `Al-Nassr`; mirror the source spelling, punctuation, hyphenation, and requested separators.
- For questions asking a person's full name, use the exact public form consistently. For country questions tied to official communiques, prefer the source's form rather than an English synonym.
- Distinguish a participant's last scheduled event from the last event actually completed; injuries, withdrawals, suspensions, and non-entry can make the earlier event decisive.
- A 20-plus-point polling lead very near a first-round election should produce a concentrated forecast even when the runoff remains competitive.
